title: Cross-component release choreography and consolidated release notes runbook for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Goal: Define a single coordinated release cadence and a consolidated release notes runbook that ties together API, Console, and Runtime component milestones, cut criteria, and GTM artifacts. Deliverables: 1) Milestone calendar with scope-lock and cut criteria per component; 2) Single release notes template (engineer + PM + design snippets); 3) Preflight checklist for legal, security, and support; 4) Post-release telemetry checklist and rollback/playbook. This ticket coordinates owners across Eng, Design, Docs, Support, Sales, and Security to ensure we hit the release window with aligned messaging and fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Milestone calendar published to Confluence and linked in Console release pipeline
Component-specific cut criteria documented and agreed by ENG leads (latency, regression tests, e2e smoke)
Consolidated release notes template approved by design and docs and populated for this train
GTM comms draft (email, changelog, customer portal) reviewed by Growth and Sales
Deployment rollback and canary gating runbook created and validated with SRE
Security and legal signoff on packaged release notes and customer-facing statements

updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff with cross-functional leads. Agreed on three milestone dates targeting March sprint boundary. Initial scope lock proposal: two-week code freeze before target GA.
2025-02-12: Design reviewed initial release note layout; recommendation to split technical notes (engineer-facing) vs user-facing highlights. Action: Hannah to produce two variants by 2025-02-14.

2025-02-13: Eng triage: Runtime team proposed relaxed cut criterion for low-risk quantization changes; PM pushed back to require regression suite coverage. Trade-off: small delay vs risk of unclear regressions. Decision: require full regression pass for quantization delta >1% perplexity (documented in cut criteria).
2025-02-14: Security flagged customer-facing wording around data residency. Noor requested legal-approved phrasing; added to preflight checklist with 48h review SLA.
2025-02-16: SRE ran a dry-run of canary rollback; discovered a gap in automatic traffic-shift script. Follow-up: ENG-4231 to patch script; temporary manual rollback playbook added.
2025-02-18: Consolidated release notes draft available in Google Doc. Links and screenshots pending. Next: GTM review on 2025-02-20 and finalize release cadence signoff by eng leads on 2025-02-21.

risks: Late regression failures in runtime quantization could force scope cut that impacts Console UX features
Security/legal wording delay may prevent publishing customer-facing notes on GA day
Observability gaps for new metrics could delay confident rollback decisions
Parallel releases in adjacent trains (partner integrations) may create conflicting comms windows
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): 1% of traffic to new runtime variant for 6 hours, monitor latency/error budget (SLOs)
Phase 2 (Staggered): 10% -> 25% over 24 hours with automated checks; require green for 2 consecutive evaluation windows
Phase 3 (General): 100% with extended telemetry monitoring for 72 hours
Rollback gates: on error_rate > 3x baseline or p95 latency > SLO threshold for two windows -> rollback to previous variant
Fallback model routing: if capacity shortfall detected, route to compatible lower-cost model variant (pre-approved)
notes_for_comm: Audience segmentation: developer users (technical changelog) vs product users (what's new summary)
Timing: coordinate public changelog publish immediately after GA signoff and internal comms 1 hour prior
Sales: prepare FAQ and upgrade guidance; emphasize cost/latency improvements and migration steps
Support: prepare canned responses for common upgrade questions and known limitations
Metrics to highlight in external comms: median latency improvement, unit-cost delta, availability SLA
